title: The Rani of Jhansi
text:
Lakshmibai married Gangadhar Rao, the raja of Jhansi in central India. Shortly before he died in 1853 the couple adopted a boy as heir. The British East India Company refused to recognize the adoption and annexed Jhansi under the "doctrine of lapse". The widowed Rani was pensioned off.

In 1857 a great rebellion spread across northern India. In Jhansi, mutinous soldiers killed British officers and civilians. The Rani took control of the state and organized its defense. In March 1858 a British force under Sir Hugh Rose besieged the city. The Rani directed the defense from the fort, and the city held out for about two weeks before it was stormed. She escaped at night with a small escort.

She joined the rebel leader Tatya Tope, and together they seized the fortress of Gwalior. In June 1858, fighting at the head of her cavalry near Gwalior, she was killed. She was in her twenties.

Rose is reported to have called her the bravest and best of the rebel military leaders. In India she became a lasting symbol of resistance.
lesson: Courage and capacity in a crisis do not wait for title or permission. Lead with what you have when the moment demands it.
people: Rani Lakshmibai, Sir Hugh Rose, Tatya Tope
source: British military reports, including Sir Hugh Rose's dispatches; Indian histories of the 1857 rebellion
caveat: Some popular details, such as her escape with her son tied to her back, and her exact role in the 1857 killings at Jhansi, are disputed.
